# Nick McCarty — Personal Website

> Technical blog and portfolio covering agentic systems engineering, LLM evaluation, computer vision, and geospatial AI.

## Author

Nick McCarty is a machine learning engineer, consultant, and technical instructor. He works at Upskilled Consulting on ML/AI projects spanning computer vision, photogrammetry, and agentic system design. He is the author of the 23-post Agentic Harness Engineering series, a comprehensive treatment of production agentic pipeline architecture grounded in empirical experiment and a structured literature review of over 60 papers.

- Email: nick@upskilled.consulting
- LinkedIn: https://linkedin.com/in/nicholasmccarty
- GitHub: https://github.com/nickmccarty

## Agentic Harness Engineering Series (Posts 1–23)

A 23-post series on the design, empirics, and literature behind production agentic pipelines. The series covers eleven subsystem patterns, four production experiments, and structured reviews of 60+ papers on LLM evaluation, planning, alignment, security, and knowledge retrieval.

### Architecture and Patterns (Posts 1–11, May 22, 2026)

URL: /blog/the-wiggum-loop.html
Title: The Wiggum Loop: Cross-Model Evaluation and Dimensional Revision
Topics: LLM evaluation, producer-evaluator separation, self-preference bias, dimensional rubric, cross-model scoring
Summary: The two-loop architecture — Ralph (outer revision) and Wiggum (inner evaluation) — that produces reliably high-quality agentic output. Includes D3.js diagrams and score trajectory data from 1,500 production runs.

URL: /blog/harness-thesis.html
Title: The Harness Thesis: Why Scaffolding Beats Model Selection
Topics: agentic scaffolding, pipeline architecture, model selection, quality engineering
Summary: The empirical case that scaffolding quality matters more than model choice for a fixed task domain. Covers the five-stage pipeline and the silent overwrite failure that motivated the project.

URL: /blog/pipeline-in-motion.html
Title: The Pipeline in Motion: Tracing a Task Through All Eleven Subsystems
Topics: pipeline architecture, task decomposition, retrieval, synthesis, JSONL, agentic systems
Summary: A single research query traced end-to-end through all eleven subsystems, with D3.js architecture diagrams at each hop.

URL: /blog/failure-taxonomy.html
Title: A Failure Taxonomy for Agentic Systems
Topics: failure analysis, agentic systems, retrieval failures, synthesis failures, evaluation failures
Summary: Six failure classes ranked by frequency and cost, with real data from 1,500 production runs and the diagnostic patterns that catch them early.

URL: /blog/inference-patterns.html
Title: Inference Patterns: The Substrate Layer
Topics: inference optimization, model routing, keep-alive, evaluator pool, LLM infrastructure
Summary: Four patterns governing how LLM calls are issued, routed, and kept warm: the Inference Shim, Model Role Separation, Evaluator Pool, and Keep-Alive Budget.

URL: /blog/context-engineering.html
Title: Context Engineering: What Reaches the Model
Topics: context management, RAG, Planner-First, Novelty Gate, semantic chunking, memory store
Summary: Five patterns governing the research half of the pipeline: Planner-First, Novelty Gate, Dual-Backend Memory Store, Semantic Chunker, and Dynamic Context Injection.

URL: /blog/verification-patterns.html
Title: Verification Patterns: Measuring and Improving Output Quality
Topics: output verification, dimensional rubric, surgical compression, ReAct, evaluation strategy
Summary: Three patterns completing the verification layer: Dimensional Rubric, Surgical Compressor, and ReAct Comparator.

URL: /blog/orchestration-patterns.html
Title: Orchestration Patterns: Scaling to Multi-Agent Execution
Topics: multi-agent systems, DAG orchestration, worktree isolation, MCP, skill registry
Summary: Four patterns for coordinating multiple agents: DAG Orchestrator, Worktree Context, MCP Dispatch Router, and Skill Registry.

URL: /blog/security-patterns.html
Title: Security Patterns: Constraining the Agent
Topics: agentic security, AST analysis, path sandboxing, prompt injection defense, CDP guard
Summary: Four security patterns implemented with Python stdlib: AST Guard, Path Sandbox, Injection Scanner, and CDP Guard.

URL: /blog/observability-flywheel.html
Title: Observability and the Data Flywheel
Topics: observability, tracing, JSONL logging, data flywheel, RL rollout, self-improvement
Summary: Six patterns closing the feedback loop: RunTrace, JSONL Audit Log, Chrome Trace Exporter, Data Flywheel, RL Rollout, and Literature Review Pipeline.

URL: /blog/parallel-inference.html
Title: Parallel Inference: Hardware Substrates for LLM Workloads
Topics: GPU architecture, llama.cpp, vLLM, GGUF, quantization, KV cache, parallel processing
Summary: GPU memory hierarchy, SM architecture, llama.cpp, vLLM, GGUF quantization, and KV cache pressure — the hardware realities that determine whether an agentic pipeline is fast or broken.

### Experiments and Alignment (Posts 12 & 14, May 23, 2026)

URL: /blog/experimental-methodology.html
Title: Experimental Methodology: Four Experiments, One Pipeline
Topics: experimental design, CRD, evaluator ceiling, producer ceiling, synthesis instructions, ablation
Summary: Four completely randomized designs that exposed the evaluator ceiling, the producer ceiling, and the synthesis instruction bottleneck that neither model upgrade could fix.

URL: /blog/multi-objective-alignment.html
Title: Multi-Objective Alignment: Beyond Scalar Rewards
Topics: RLHF, multi-objective optimization, DPA, MO-ODPO, MGDA, safety fine-tuning, reward modeling
Summary: DPA, MO-ODPO, MGDA-Decoupled, and the safety fine-tuning hazard: high dataset similarity degrades safety by 10.33%.

### Small Language Models (Post 15, May 8, 2026)

URL: /blog/slm-efficiency.html
Title: Small Language Models and the Efficiency-Accuracy Frontier
Topics: SLM, small language models, efficiency, benchmarking, energy, model selection, multi-model architecture
Summary: SLM-Bench across 15 models, 9 tasks, 4 hardware configs. Accuracy and energy efficiency don't co-optimize — model selection is a portfolio problem, not a ranking problem.

### Literature Reviews — Tools, Knowledge Graphs, Security, Fine-Tuning (Posts 16, 18, 20–21, May 1, 2026)

URL: /blog/tool-use-planning.html
Title: Agentic Tool Use and Planning: What the Literature Says
Topics: tool use, LLM planning, NL2Plan, PEARL, ToolTree, ToolRet, safety bypass, multi-LLM
Summary: NL2Plan, PEARL, ToolTree, ToolRet, Memory-as-a-Tool, and a 92% safety bypass rate — fifteen papers on LLM planning and tool use.

URL: /blog/knowledge-graphs-extraction.html
Title: Knowledge Graphs and Structured Extraction: Beyond the Vector Store
Topics: knowledge graphs, structured extraction, semantic graphs, MeXtract, RAG, graph retrieval
Summary: Document semantic graphs outperform flat-list retrieval. MeXtract achieves SOTA metadata extraction with 0.5B parameters.

URL: /blog/prompt-injection-security.html
Title: Prompt Injection and Agentic Security: What the Attack Literature Says
Topics: prompt injection, adversarial attacks, HouYi, gradient-based injection, Prompt Infection, multi-agent security
Summary: HouYi compromises 86% of real LLM applications. Gradient-based injections bypass pattern-matching by design. Prompt Infection replicates virally through multi-agent DAGs.

URL: /blog/alignment-fine-tuning.html
Title: Fine-Tuning and Alignment Deep Cuts: Synthetic Data, Poisoning, and Safety Recovery
Topics: fine-tuning, RLHF, synthetic data, data poisoning, safety recovery, FLR, SFT, perplexity
Summary: FLR matches GPT-4-annotated reward models without human annotation. Label-flipping poisoning as convex optimization. Harmful rate drops 33.25% to 1.74% via weight restoration.

### Literature Reviews — Evaluation, Judges, and Knowledge Queries (Posts 13, 17, 19, 22–23, April 29, 2026)

URL: /blog/judge-reliability.html
Title: Judging the Judges: Benchmark Contamination and Evaluation Reliability
Topics: LLM-as-a-judge, evaluation reliability, position bias, benchmark contamination, self-preference
Summary: Best judges lag human agreement by 5 points. Eight of nine judges show always-A position bias. What the reliability literature means for harness design.

URL: /blog/evaluation-uncertainty.html
Title: Evaluation Uncertainty, Calibration, and Harness Reliability
Topics: uncertainty quantification, conformal prediction, calibration, ConFix, Agent-as-a-Judge, hallucination
Summary: Conformal prediction turns point scores into calibrated intervals. Fact-level ConFix reduces hallucinations without retrieval. Agent-as-a-Judge outperforms LLM-as-a-Judge.

URL: /blog/evaluation-robustness.html
Title: Automated Evaluation Robustness: Metamorphic Testing, Scoring Bias, and Prompt Sensitivity
Topics: metamorphic testing, LLMORPH, scoring bias, prompt sensitivity, rubric design, LLM evaluation
Summary: LLMORPH finds evaluator inconsistencies across 561,000 test executions. Three novel scoring biases — rubric order, score ID, reference answer — originate in prompt design.

URL: /blog/structured-knowledge-queries.html
Title: Structured Knowledge Queries: Ontology, SPARQL, and Grounded Verification
Topics: SPARQL, ontology, knowledge graphs, ODA, GRASP, ETLCH, chain of verification, Wikidata
Summary: ODA improves LLM+KG accuracy by 12.87% via recursive observation-action-reflection. GRASP achieves zero-shot SPARQL SOTA on Wikidata without fine-tuning.

URL: /blog/judge-benchmarks-scaling.html
Title: Judge Benchmarks and Test-Time Scaling: Where LLM Judges Succeed and Where They Don't
Topics: JETTS, Omni-MATH, M-JudgeBench, IF-RewardBench, test-time scaling, process reward models, reranking
Summary: JETTS: judges match outcome reward models for reranking but lose to process reward models in beam search. Omni-Judge is wrong in 96.4% of expert disagreements.

## Key Topics

- **Agentic Systems**: Harness engineering, multi-agent orchestration, producer-evaluator loops, DAG execution, MCP
- **LLM Evaluation**: Judge reliability, position bias, calibration, conformal prediction, metamorphic testing, benchmark design
- **Alignment and Fine-Tuning**: RLHF, multi-objective optimization, synthetic data, data poisoning, safety recovery
- **Security**: Prompt injection attacks, agentic sandboxing, adversarial inputs, multi-agent attack propagation
- **Knowledge Retrieval**: RAG, knowledge graphs, SPARQL, ontology, structured extraction, grounded verification
- **Computer Vision**: Object detection, image segmentation, feature extraction, mechanistic interpretability
- **Foundation Models**: SAM, vision transformers, Faster R-CNN, LoRA, PEFT
- **Geospatial AI**: Drone imagery, orthomosaics, GeoTIFF processing, coordinate systems, photogrammetry
- **Hardware and Inference**: GPU architecture, llama.cpp, vLLM, quantization, KV cache optimization
- **Small Language Models**: Efficiency frontiers, multi-model architectures, energy benchmarking

## Technical Stack

- Python, PyTorch for deep learning and pipeline engineering
- Faster R-CNN, SAM for object detection and segmentation
- llama.cpp, vLLM for local LLM inference
- rasterio for geospatial data processing
- FastAPI for web services
- D3.js for interactive data visualization
- Leaflet for web mapping
